images.filename: Declaration of Independence (1819), by John Trumbull.jpg
images.caption: John Trumbull's painting, Declaration of Independence, depicting the five-man drafting committee of the Declaration of Independence presenting their work to the Congress. The painting can be found on the back of the U.S. $2 bill. The original hangs in the US Capitol rotunda. It does not represent a real ceremony; the characters portrayed were never in the same room at the same time.
images.alt: John Trumbull's painting, Declaration of Independence, depicting the five-man drafting committee of the Declaration of Independence presenting their work to the Congress. images.caption: Eastern Market, located at the intersection of 7th and C Streets, S.E., in the Capitol Hill neighborhood of Washington, D.C. images.filename: QR CC cenotaphs Tip and Hale.JPG
images.caption: Cenotpahs of Congressional leaders, Tip O'Neill (front) and Hale Boggs (back - both marked by flags).  Both are true cenotaphs (not graves).  The Boggs memorial is in the form of a "Latrobe cenotaph" which is used exclusively at the Congressional Cemetery (a National Historic Landmark), almost exclusively for Congressmen.  Boggs shares his cenotaph with Nick Begich (text on other side) - they were lost together in a plane crash in Alaska.

images.filename: USS Bon Homme Richard (CVA-31) underway in the Gulf of Tonkin on 2 November 1964.jpg
images.caption:
The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Bon Homme Richard (CVA-31) underway in the South China Sea / Western Pacific, late 1964. The carrier, with Carrier Air Wing 19 (CVW-19) embarked, was deployed to the Western Pacific from 28 January to 21 November 1964. 

Note: The photo is often captioned as being taken in the Gulf of Tonkin on 2 November 1964. However, according to the ship’s official deck log, the USS Bon Homme Richard was still moored in Yokosuka, Japan on the morning of 2 November 1964 and only got underway in the afternoon. The photo was most likely taken later in November 1964 after the ship had reached the operational area.
images.alt:
The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Bon Homme Richard (CVA-31) underway in the South China Sea / Western Pacific, late 1964. The carrier, with Carrier Air Wing 19 (CVW-19) embarked, was deployed to the Western Pacific from 28 January to 21 November 1964. 

Note: The photo is often captioned as being taken in the Gulf of Tonkin on 2 November 1964. However, according to the ship’s official deck log, the USS Bon Homme Richard was still moored in Yokosuka, Japan on the morning of 2 November 1964 and only got underway in the afternoon. The photo was most likely taken later in November 1964 after the ship had reached the operational area.
